name: Role-based staff access
description: The system must support distinct permissions for managers, cashiers, kitchen staff, and supervisors, with role-specific access to orders, refunds, and operational controls.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks who can open tills, refund orders, or change menu pricing.
Developer asks about staff roles and permission boundaries.
Developer mentions accountability and audit trails for sales actions.

name: Multi-location operations
description: The system must support more than one restaurant location or service site while keeping orders, pricing, and team reporting consistent and separate by branch.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks whether there are multiple sites or branches.
Developer asks how inventory, pricing, or reports are kept separate by location.
Developer mentions location-level comparisons or branch performance.

name: Menu and inventory tracking
description: The system must handle menu items, stock levels, ingredient usage, and low-stock warnings so the kitchen can avoid sellouts and waste.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about stock controls or item availability.
Developer discusses ingredients, recipe usage, or expiration risks.
Developer mentions low-stock alerts or waste prevention.

name: Order flow and kitchen handoff
description: The system must support order intake, table or ticket tracking, kitchen communication, and status updates so the workflow stays accurate and fast.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks how orders are captured and sent to the kitchen.
Developer mentions tickets, table service, or status tracking.
Developer discusses order accuracy or peak-time service flow.

name: Payment and reconciliation
description: The system must support cash, card, and digital payments with end-of-day settlement and reconciliation to reduce shortfalls and manual checks.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about payment methods or tipping.
Developer asks how sales are reconciled at closing.
Developer mentions cash drawers, card settlement, or daily totals.

name: Reporting and operational dashboards
description: The business needs sales, item performance, staffing, and service metrics to understand demand and operational issues across shifts and locations.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about sales reports, shift dashboards, or item performance.
Developer mentions staffing visibility or service trends.
Developer discusses operational KPIs for management.

name: Supplier and purchasing workflow
description: The business needs purchasing records, supplier pricing, and restocking planning to keep core ingredients available without unnecessary waste.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about supplier records or reorder planning.
Developer mentions ingredient restocking or purchase orders.
Developer discusses cost control or procurement.

name: Customer and loyalty retention needs
description: The system must support customer details, repeat purchase patterns, and loyalty or promotion tracking without creating friction at checkout.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about customer records or loyalty.
Developer mentions repeat purchase behavior or promotions.
Developer discusses retention or personalized offers.

name: Operational constraints and integrations
description: The solution must fit real restaurant operations, likely with existing accounting or POS tools, low training overhead, and minimal downtime during business hours.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about integrations with current tools.
Developer mentions training burden, staff adoption, or downtime risk.
Developer discusses low-friction operations during service.
